ol.li: pnpm creates a hidden folder inside our project node modules -> node_modules/.pnpm. This is here the actual contents live. one subfolder per exact package version (for all dependencies, devdependencies and even for nested dependencies etc)

For each package version, pnpm reads the package's index files and every entry, Hardlinks the corresponding content hash file from store/v11/files/xx/... into the node_modules/.pnpm/packageNmae@version

li.span: Now pnpm links the top-level dependencies in our project main node_modules via symlinks
Nested/transitive dependencies also symlink to its respective hardLinked folder created in node_modules/.pnpm

div.font: Why cant pnpm directly hardlink in the main node_modules folder for all the packages: -

li.font: Hardlinking the files for every packages will also require hardlinking the files for the nested dependencies and that too for that same packages also, and because hardlinking can only be done for files and not folder this would slower the process

Now if u r thinking to hardlink one package and then symlink that package for others requiring it, then in this case there will be technical and architectural problems like maintaining the first hardlinked package path and also if we uninstall one dependency which had the hardlinked package then this will make that hardlinked package invalid for every packages that was symlinked to this hardlinked package

ol.li: Pnpm fetches hte new version's metadata/tarball and verifies integrity
For each file in that tarball, it ocmputes the content hash
checks: does the file wiith this exact hash already exist in the store,
if yes, then it skip writing it, just reusee the existing stored file (hardlink it into node_module/.pnpm when needed)
if No, then it write this new file into the store under its calculated new hash

div.font: 1. pnpm dlx: - alias cmds pnx, pnpx

span.font: When we dont want to install the package permanently, and using it temporarily
If the packages already exists in the store it will use that, else pnpm will download the package in sperate folder and not in the files folder
Bydefualt dlx packags expiry time is 24hrs
we can modify this defualt expiry time via config file
pnpm creates a temporary hash named folder for this dlx package at ~/.cache/pnpm/dlx, this hash folder contains the package.json file with its package name
packages building/linking of these packages happens at (pending)
Bin file of these packages are (pending)
Pnpm calculates the remaining expiry time of these dlx package by comparing cache hash folder creation time(file system timestamp) with the max-expiry-set in the config file
The meta data of these packages are store in ~/.cache/pnpm/dlx folder

li.font: On pnpm remove, it will only delink, the package from the current project, and wont delete the package from the store
So claim the disk space, we will have to explicitly run the prune cmd, it will delete all the packages that is not refrenced by any project and the dlx packages that has expired

div.div: pnpm still has to download the tarball from the registry (npm registry doesn't let you fetch individual files from a package). It always downloads and unpacks the full tarball into memory/temp. But when it's time to write files into the store / link them into node_modules, that's where the dedup kicks in — unchanged files skip the write-to-disk step and just get relinked, and the actual node_modules population is hardlinks either way, not copies. So the savings are mainly in disk space and node_modules population speed, not network bandwidth (there are some registry-level tricks for reducing download size too, but that's separate from the store's content-addressing).

li.font: Before downloading: pnpm fetches the metadata of the package from the npm registry. This metadata includes the hash in data.integrity field
Now pnpm check if any package with that same hash already exists in index.db, If yes then skip downloading that package tarball and reuse that
If no, then pnpm downloads package tarball and calculates the tarball hash to verify integrity.
On success verificaiton pnpm then calculates the hashes of the files in that package to organize the content-addressable store.

For each resolved package version, checks if the hash already exists in index.db, If yes then skip downloading tarball and reuse that (reused)
If no, then pnpm downloads package tarball and calculates the tarball hash to verify integrity, unpack -> hash each file (downloaded)
Link everything into this projects node_modules/.pnpm (added)

li.font: const hash = "00cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944..."; // just computed from file bytes of a file
const dirName = hash.slice(0, 2); // "00" <- This file will go in this directory
const fileName = hash.slice(2); // rest of hash will be the name of that file
const fullPath = `store/v11/files/00/cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944...`; // And it will be stored like this, So the full file hash is calculated as dir Hash + file Hash
